Title: Electrical power system for SRMSAT-3: An autonomous rendezvous and docking mission
Source title: Proceedings of the International Astronautical Congress, IAC
Abstract: Autonomous docking of Nanosatellites opens up a broad scope of opportunities for space exploration in future, such as in-orbit servicing, scientific and technological experiments and collaborative building of space stations using small modules. This mission will consume maximum power for Attitude Determination and Control System, Propulsion System, Autonomous Guidance and Navigation, Intersatellite Communication, all bounding within the Mechanical and Structural constraints. Electrical Power System (EPS) for SRMSAT-3 plays a vital role primarily to fulfil the demands for reaction wheels and secondary thrusters to control orientation and position during the Docking phase and for inter-satellite communication when in close proximity with the Target. The Mission SRMSAT-3 intends to dock autonomously, a Chaser with the Target satellite in the near-earth circular orbit at approximately 500 km altitude. The EPS is required to generate, store and distribute a large amount of power by designing efficient solar panels and battery units to meet the estimated power budget which was brought down to 30 Watts for the Chaser Satellite and Target being much lower. Hence, the usage of efficient Multi-junction solar cells is employed in deployable and body-mounted solar panels on the Chaser and only body-mounted panels on Target. The power stored in the Battery Pack from solar panels would not be sufficient to perform on-board tasks and docking simultaneously. Hence, we compensate this by adding extra battery capacity, once the batteries are fully charged the Docking phase will be initiated. The battery configuration meets the power demand for Docking and On-board tasks during the eclipse without adding excessive solar panels on the Chaser due to size and mass constraints. The architecture includes Maximum Power Point Trackers (MPPT) to draw out maximum power from solar panels to the power bus for further distribution. The Protection unit will perform tasks by using switchable components, limit excess power to avoid damages and increase the efficiency of the bus. Moreover, it is tailored in such a way that it could perform essential on-board tasks systematically even in the extreme conditions by entering a safe mode and not shutting down completely. It was found that with a few adjustments & modifications, the proposed EPS can be successfully implemented to realize the mission objectives of SRMSAT-3. © 2020 by the International Astronautical Federation (IAF).
